short_summary: The Drama Creek Estates board held its regular October meeting, approving an $18,400 landscaping contract for the front entrance, rejecting a proposal to extend pool hours, hearing a homeowner streetlight complaint, and briefly entering executive session to discuss a delinquent account before adjourning.
executive_summary: The board convened with all five directors present, establishing quorum. The treasurer reported roughly $42,000 in operating funds and $85,000 in reserves, noting landscaping was running about $3,000 over budget. The board heard a proposal from Lone Star Landscaping to replace dead shrubs and upgrade irrigation at the front entrance for $18,400, which was approved unanimously. A motion to extend pool hours on Fridays and Saturdays through the end of October failed 2-3 amid concerns about noise complaints from nearby homeowners. During homeowner comments, a resident raised a concern about a prolonged streetlight outage, which the community manager agreed to address. Several follow-up items were noted, including sending the signed landscaping contract, a newsletter reminder about pool rules, and revisiting the landscaping budget at next month's budget workshop. The board then went into executive session to discuss a delinquent account; no substantive content from that session is recorded here. The meeting was adjourned at 7:51 PM.

discussion_topics.minutes_note: The treasurer reported approximately $42,000 in the operating account and $85,000 in the reserve account, and noted that landscaping spending is running approximately $3,000 over budget for the year.

discussion_topics.topic: Lone Star Landscaping front entrance proposal
discussion_topics.minutes_note: A representative of Lone Star Landscaping presented a proposal to replace dead shrubs and upgrade the irrigation controller at the front entrance for $18,400, with work proposed to begin the week of November 9. The board discussed the warranty status of the existing and proposed irrigation controllers before voting.
The board discussed a proposal to extend pool hours to 10 PM on Fridays and Saturdays through the end of October, including concerns about noise complaints from nearby homeowners on Ripple Lane.
A homeowner on Willow Bend reported that the streetlight at Willow Bend and Creekside had been out for three weeks.
The board went into executive session to discuss a delinquent account. No other matters were addressed in executive session.
